pr_body:
Add a `MaxDepth` property to `JsonWriterOptions` and ensures that `JsonSerializerOptions.MaxDepth` flows to `Utf8JsonWriter` in serialization.

Fix #44947.

issue_context.title: Add MaxDepth to JsonWriterOptions
comments: I've updated the API proposal and marked it ready for review.

review_comments:
Backwards compat would imply 1000 for write (and 64 for read).

Technically, this is a breaking change for those that write JSON > 64 levels but do not read that JSON back; for those that read and write the same JSON, the serializer's MaxDepth (either the default value or the value set explicitly) would be fine.

> Backwards compat would imply 1000 for write (and 64 for read).

Currently `JsonSerializer` forces a max depth of 64 when writing (unless a nonzero `JsonSerializerOptions.MaxDepth` setting is specified). This is a [check separate to the `Utf8JsonWriter` layer](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2b1f420cca78ca03f867caa68f30cf81ae2b4187/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonConverterOfT.cs#L323).
Ah that's right I forgot the serializer checks for that. Can we now remove that logic and let the writer throw?

Good question. The converter check is certainly redundant (and a bit hit-or-miss, see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/50321#issuecomment-892695769) so removing it would an improvement. The problem though is that the converter throws a `JsonException` with a message indicating the presence of a potential cycle whereas the `Utf8JsonWriter` throws an [`InvalidOperationException`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Writer/Utf8JsonWriter.cs#L430) which will get [wrapped in a `JsonException`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0749730dbbe7e9815d99839c3b9333ea409ba98f/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonConverterOfT.ReadCore.cs#L89) by the serializer. 

I don't think making that change would be a huge break. cc @layomia for a second opinion.

I pushed commit 0e430928c8d84288e0b2cb2e1d1726087f905ae8 that introduces the change. However I feel that from a user experience perspective this is a regression. The error message changes from `Possible object cycle detected` to `The object or value could not be serialized` with an inner exception containing the actual message `CurrentDepth (64) is equal to or larger than the maximum allowed depth of 64. Cannot write the next JSON object or array.`
Can we modify the `InvalidOperationException` message thrown by the writer to say something like "If called from the serializer, {cycle message}".
I do like the 2 `if` statements that were removed from the serializer's write() method.

> Can we modify the InvalidOperationException message thrown by the writer to say something like "If called from the serializer, {cycle message}".

I don't believe the writer is able to distinguish this. We'd probably need to handle the exception and change it, but that feels awkward. To be honest I think we should just keep the existing duplication.

I reverted https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/61608/commits/0e430928c8d84288e0b2cb2e1d1726087f905ae8, since I wasn't satisfied with the quality of the error messages. We can revisit in a separate PR.

Is it verified anywhere that MaxDepth of `1` and `2` works consistently for read and write? i.e. the reader and writer have the same semantics. Also, depending on the viewpoint, a depth of `1` may not imply any object\array support.

Yes. Ultimately, the semantics stem from the semantics of the `Utf8JsonWriter/Reader.CurrentDepth` properties, which are consistent and we already have testing for those:

1. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0749730dbbe7e9815d99839c3b9333ea409ba98f/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/tests/System.Text.Json.Tests/Utf8JsonReaderTests.cs
2. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/tests/System.Text.Json.Tests/Utf8JsonWriterTests.cs

Namely, a depth of 0 is denotes a root-level value. The meaning of `MaxDepth` being set to `0` is special, and in `JsonWriterOptions` it specifically mirrors the semantics of `Utf8JsonReader`.
